about.title: The engineer behind the practice
about.lead: I build software that has to work in production — not demos that impress in a meeting and collapse under real usage.
about.p1: I am Hamza Shahid, a full-stack software engineer and AI systems architect with over three years spent building scalable web applications, AI-powered platforms, and enterprise-grade backend infrastructure. My work spans system architecture, API design, database engineering, cloud deployment, and the applied AI layer — retrieval pipelines, LLM integration, and automation that produces results a business can rely on.
about.p2: Most of my engagements start where something is already at risk: a prototype that cannot be taken to customers, a backend buckling under growth, or an AI feature that sounds convincing but is not accurate enough to ship. I take responsibility for the whole path — deciding the architecture, writing the code, deploying it, and staying accountable for how it behaves once real users arrive.
about.p3: I work with a small number of clients at a time, deliberately. Founders and product teams get a direct line to the person doing the engineering, written technical reasoning behind every significant decision, and systems their own team can operate long after the engagement ends.

projects.title: Case studies with measured outcomes
projects.subtitle: A sample of systems taken from problem statement to production. Client names are withheld under confidentiality; architecture and results are described as delivered.

items.title: Enterprise AI Knowledge Assistant
items.challenge: A services company was losing senior staff hours to repetitive internal questions buried across years of policy documents, contracts, and process guides that keyword search could not surface reliably.
items.approach: Designed a retrieval-augmented assistant over a vector-indexed document corpus with hybrid retrieval, permission-aware filtering, mandatory source citation, and an offline evaluation suite that gates every prompt and model change before release.

items.title: Multi-Vendor Commerce Platform
items.challenge: A retail operator was running catalog, orders, and vendor payouts across spreadsheets and disconnected tools, which capped growth and made reconciliation a recurring monthly failure.
items.approach: Built a unified commerce platform with vendor onboarding, catalog and inventory management, role-based permissions, payment and refund flows, order lifecycle automation, and an operations dashboard reporting on live transactional data.

impact.label: Transaction volume processed in year one

items.title: Enterprise Backend & Access Control Platform
items.challenge: A growing SaaS product had authorization logic scattered across its codebase, no reliable audit trail, and an API that buckled during peak usage — blocking an enterprise security review.
items.approach: Re-architected the backend around a centralized permission model with JWT authentication, granular role-based access control, immutable audit logging, background job processing, request-level caching, and versioned API contracts.

impact.label: p95 response time under peak load

items.title: AI-Driven Business Automation Platform
items.challenge: An operations team was spending most of each week manually routing requests, chasing approvals, and assembling reports from four systems that did not talk to each other.
items.approach: Delivered an automation platform combining event-driven workflow orchestration, LLM-based classification and summarization, exception queues for human review, and scheduled report generation across previously siloed data sources.

items.title: Real-Time Analytics & Reporting Layer
items.challenge: Leadership decisions were running a day behind the business because reporting queries ran directly against a transactional database, degrading application performance whenever anyone opened a dashboard.
items.approach: Introduced a separated analytical layer with incremental aggregation, materialized rollups, query-level caching, and an API purpose-built for dashboard access patterns, removing reporting load from the production write path entirely.

items.title: AI Document Intelligence for Compliance Review
items.challenge: A compliance function was manually reading long third-party documents to extract a fixed set of fields — slow, inconsistent between reviewers, and impossible to scale with rising volume.
items.approach: Built a document intelligence pipeline pairing layout-aware parsing with structured LLM extraction, per-field confidence scoring, and a review interface that routes only low-confidence extractions to a human specialist.

impact.label: Field extraction accuracy on validation set
